landing.title: Know exactly how your team uses Codex
landing.subtitle: A menu bar app that reads your local Codex sessions and a realtime team dashboard: tokens, cache hits, model mix and what it would cost at API prices.
landing.installHint: Works on macOS and Windows (native and WSL2). Sign in with Google or GitHub.

menubar.title: Menu bar app
menubar.body: Live daily totals, tokens per second for the running session, model breakdown and a usage heatmap — right in your menu bar or system tray.

team.title: Team dashboard
team.body: Organizations map to your Clerk org. Compare members, see active hours and weekday patterns, and spot who is live right now.

realtime.title: Realtime by design
realtime.body: Devices sync hourly buckets to Convex; every chart updates the moment new usage lands. Stored in UTC, shown in your local time.

cost.title: API-equivalent cost
cost.body: Subscription usage priced at standard OpenAI API list prices, with cache-hit savings called out — so you know what the plan is worth.

how.1: Install the npm package and run `codex-tracker login`.
how.2: Approve the device in this dashboard with your Google or GitHub account.
how.3: Usage is read from local Codex session logs and synced every minute.

landing.footer: Built for Codex CLI · Next.js · Convex · Clerk

access.1: Upload hourly token usage and session summaries from that machine to your account.
access.2: Read your own usage across devices (to merge its heatmap).
access.3: It cannot read other members' data or change your organization.

settings.connectBody: Install the npm package on each machine and point it at this dashboard:
settings.connectStep2: Sign in (opens this dashboard to approve the device)
settings.connectStep3: Run in the background — the tray icon shows today's usage; on WSL2 use the headless agent
settings.pricingBody: Costs are computed on each device from standard OpenAI API list prices, including the long-context tier above 272K input tokens. Only Codex (OpenAI) usage is reported — other providers your agents may use are not counted. Newer models fall back to the closest known family and are marked as estimated.
